item.title: Montrealers in Qatar look for a way out as Ottawa plans Mideast evacuations
item.description: "If the Canadian government arranges for evacuation, I'm on that flight," says Maher Chebib. "Because we're not hearing anything from Canada, a lot of us are booking self-evacuations."

item.title: Defamation trial: Woman says Cardinal Ouellet touched her inappropriately
item.description: The retired cardinal is suing Paméla Groleau, a former pastoral agent with the Quebec City diocese, for $100,000 for allegations she made about him.

item.title: Agitator Yves Engler sentenced to probation for harassing Montreal police investigator
item.description: Engler's website included a form letter with the police investigator's email address, leading to a flood of messages in her inbox.

item.title: Montreal police arrest Bryan Fuentes Gramajo, Canada's most wanted fugitive
item.description: The 24-year-old was wanted on a Canada-wide arrest warrant in connection with a fatal shooting at a Toronto shopping centre parking lot.

item.title: Cowan: No-trade clause was key for family-focused Canadien Mike Matheson
item.description: Veteran defenceman loves playing for Habs and has strong roots in Montreal, which is why he insisted on no-movement clause in new contract.

item.title: Alouettes toss play-calling reins to quarterback great Anthony Calvillo
item.description: Ready to take the next step in his coaching journey, legendary pivot will be responsible for Montreal's offensive attack this season.

item.title: Recall issued for ground beef sold at Pierrefonds grocery store
item.description: The products in question list Feb. 24, 2026, as the packaging date, and were only sold at Intermarché Palumbo Pierrefonds.

item.title: Longueuil man with gunshot wound shows up at hospital
item.description: It is the second victim with gunshot wounds to take himself to the hospital on Thursday.

item.title: 'Enough is enough': Chinatown residents demand moratorium on new services for the marginalized
item.description: "It is time to stop making Chinatown a dumping ground for misery," as a resource centre for sex workers is planned for the neighbourhood.

item.title: 'Is it necessary?': Montreal realtor's English Facebook posts flagged by language watchdog
item.description: Mario Conte then tried to seek guidance from the OQLF, but said his calls went unanswered.
